stories.h: Former FCT minister Jumoke Akinjide returns to politics, backs Tinubu and APC in Oyo
stories.p: Former Minister of State for the FCT Jumoke Akinjide has reportedly announced her return to active politics, declaring support for President Tinubu and the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State, Senator Sharafadeen Alli. She was previously a PDP figure.
body: Former Minister of State for the Federal Capital Territory, Oloye Jumoke Akinjide, has announced her return to active politics ahead of the 2027 general elections, and has thrown her weight behind the All Progressives Congress (APC).
## The announcement

In a statement issued on her behalf by her special assistant, Olatundun Gabriel, on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, Akinjide's team thanked her supporters for their loyalty and patience and said a new phase of political engagement had begun. The statement reportedly declared her support for President Bola Tinubu's Renewed Hope agenda and for the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State, Senator Sharafadeen Alli. Her team urged supporters across the state to stay united as she resumes political activity.
## Background

Akinjide served as Minister of State for the FCT under President Goodluck Jonathan and was a prominent member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Oyo State. Her move adds to a series of political realignments in Oyo, where Governor Seyi Makinde is completing his second term and is now the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement. Several officials have recently left Makinde's government, including a commissioner and two other appointees who resigned on Monday.
## Why it matters

Oyo is one of the largest states in the South West, and the governorship seat will be open in 2027. The APC hopes defections like Akinjide's will help it win back the state, while the PDP and other parties insist they remain strong.

stories.h: Tompolo's pro-Tinubu movement launches in Ogun with 26 campaign vehicles
stories.p: The PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, led by Government Ekpemupolo (Tompolo), has reportedly launched its Ogun chapter and donated 26 vehicles for grassroots campaigning. Ogun APC governorship candidate Solomon Adeola said stakeholders are targeting two million votes for Tinubu.
body: A pro-Tinubu campaign group backed by former Niger Delta militant leader Government Oweizide Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has launched its Ogun State chapter and donated 26 campaign vehicles, according to reports.
## The launch

The PBAT Door-to-Door Movement held the inauguration on Friday, 30 October 2026, at the Ake Palace Arcade in Abeokuta, attended by politicians, government officials and supporters of President Bola Tinubu. Representing Tompolo, High Chief Kestin Pondi, managing director of Tantita Security Services, said the vehicles would be deployed across Ogun State's 26 constituencies for community outreach and voter mobilisation. He described the President's economic reforms as important steps for national development.
## What was said

Governor Dapo Abiodun, represented by his deputy, Noimot Salako-Oyedele, praised the movement's contribution to political engagement in the state. The APC governorship candidate, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, said political stakeholders were aiming to deliver at least two million votes for Tinubu in Ogun in the 2027 presidential election. The movement's national coordinator, Sunday Asuku, said it would work with other support groups.
## Background

Tompolo's company, Tantita Security Services, holds a federal contract to protect oil pipelines in the Niger Delta, and the government credits it with helping to reduce oil theft. Ogun is the home state of former President Olusegun Obasanjo and borders Lagos, Tinubu's political base. APC supporters say such groups help the party reach voters at the grassroots.
more: The movement donated 26 vehicles for Ogun's 26 constituencies.
Adeola says stakeholders target two million votes for Tinubu.
Tompolo's firm holds a federal pipeline security contract.

stories.h: Femi Adebayo opens cinema at his Euphoria 360 Hub, offers free screenings
stories.p: Actor Femi Adebayo has announced that the cinema at his new Euphoria 360 Hub in Lagos opens on Saturday, 7 November. The first 15 guests will be invited to the premiere of 'Jagun Jagun 2', and 45 more will get a free movie with popcorn and drinks.
body: Nollywood actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo is set to open the cinema at his newly launched Euphoria 360 Hub in Lagos, and he is offering free treats to the first visitors.
## The offer

In a video posted on Monday, 2 November 2026, Adebayo invited the public to the opening on Saturday, 7 November, at 6pm. He said the first 15 people to arrive would receive invitations to the premiere of his upcoming film 'Jagun Jagun 2', scheduled for 2 December. A further 45 people would get to watch a movie for free, with complimentary popcorn and drinks.
## Stars expected
According to the actor, guests will be able to watch alongside some well-known entertainers, including actress Bimbo Ademoye and actor Timini Egbuson.
## Background

Femi Adebayo is one of Nollywood's leading actors and producers. His epic 'Jagun Jagun', released on Netflix in 2023, became one of the platform's most-watched Nigerian titles, and a sequel has been widely anticipated. He also produced and starred in the hit film 'King of Thieves'. The Euphoria 360 Hub adds to a growing number of entertainment venues opened by Nigerian filmmakers looking to bring audiences closer to their work. The actor was among the Nollywood stars who attended the opening of Sola Sobowale's elderly care home in Ibadan this week.
## How fans reacted
Many fans said they would turn up early to secure a place, while others congratulated the actor on the new venture.
more: The cinema opens on Saturday, 7 November, at 6pm.
The first 15 guests get invitations to the 'Jagun Jagun 2' premiere.
45 more get a free movie with popcorn and drinks.

stories.h: "Go and work, I have children to take care of!": GehGeh sends strong message to his siblings and critics
stories.p: Social media personality and financial adviser GehGeh has told his brothers and sisters to work hard and stop depending entirely on him, saying he has children to care for. His message has reopened a familiar debate about the pressure Nigerian families put on relatives who become successful.
body: Popular Nigerian social media personality and financial adviser GehGeh has stirred reactions online after sending a strong message to his family members and to those who believe he should carry the financial responsibilities of everyone around him.
## "Go and work"
Speaking openly about the pressure that comes with financial success, GehGeh made it clear that having money does not mean one person should become the permanent provider for an entire family.
According to him, his brothers and sisters must learn to work hard and take responsibility for their own lives rather than depending entirely on him.
"If you're my brother or my sister, go and work. Don't depend only on me because I have children I need to take care of. I can't do more than my power for family members," he said.
## A familiar Nigerian story
His message touches on something many Nigerians can relate to, especially those who have become financially stable while other relatives continue to struggle.

In many families, once one person starts making money, expectations begin to grow. School fees, house rent, feeding allowances, business capital and even personal expenses suddenly become that person's responsibility. Sometimes the demands never seem to end.
## Drawing the line

GehGeh appears determined to draw a line. He did not suggest that helping relatives is wrong, but his message was clear: family support should have limits, particularly when someone has children and responsibilities of their own.
His remarks also highlight the pressure successful people face from relatives who believe family ties automatically guarantee financial support.
Family members should help one another whenever they can. But should one person's success become an excuse for everyone else to stop trying?
## Over to you
Is GehGeh being too harsh on his family, or is he simply saying what many successful people are afraid to tell their relatives?
more: GehGeh told his siblings to work and not depend only on him.
He says he has children to take care of.
Many Nigerians relate to the pressure of supporting relatives.

stories.h: EFCC uncovers suspected illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals in Ogun State
stories.p: The EFCC has uncovered a suspected illegal oil refinery in Ogere, Ogun State, allegedly linked to Chinese nationals. No one was found on the premises during the raid, but investigators discovered underground tanks holding a substance suspected to be diesel.
body: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has uncovered a suspected illegal oil refinery in Ogere, Ogun State, allegedly linked to Chinese nationals.

The discovery has raised fresh concerns about illegal petroleum processing in Nigeria, especially the possibility that some operations are running quietly in places far from the country's major oil-producing areas.
## The raid
According to reports, EFCC operatives raided the facility on Saturday, 31 October 2026, but nobody was found on the premises when they arrived.
During the operation, investigators discovered underground storage tanks holding substances suspected to be diesel, suggesting the site may have been used for petroleum processing and storage.
## Sludge oil from Warri and Port Harcourt

Preliminary investigations reportedly showed that sludge oil was transported from Warri in Delta State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State to the Ogun State facility, where it was allegedly processed into petroleum products.

That detail raises an important question: how was petroleum waste moved across several states to a facility allegedly operating outside the law without attracting the attention of the relevant authorities?
## Questions for investigators

Given the size and nature of such an operation, investigators will also need to establish how long the facility had been running, who financed it and whether other individuals or companies were involved.
The EFCC has reportedly taken control of the premises while investigations continue to identify those responsible, including the alleged owners and operators.
Although Chinese nationals have been linked to the facility, the identities of those involved have not been publicly established, and the allegations remain under investigation.
## A wider problem

For many Nigerians, the discovery points to a familiar and troubling issue. While the country continues to battle crude oil theft, illegal refining and lost revenue in the petroleum sector, questions remain about how such operations are set up and kept running.
The authorities are now expected to determine the full extent of what went on at the Ogere facility and whether any laws were broken.
## The big question
Who owns this refinery, how long has it been operating, and who has been supplying the materials used there?
As the EFCC investigation continues, Nigerians will be watching to see whether those behind the suspected operation are identified and brought before the law.
more: The EFCC raided the Ogere facility on 31 October.
No one was found on the premises.
Sludge oil was reportedly brought in from Warri and Port Harcourt.

stories.h: Sanusi urges Tinubu government to stop treating talk of poverty as an attack
stories.p: Emir of Kano Muhammadu Sanusi II has reportedly told the Tinubu administration to stop issuing statements from the Villa against people who raise concerns about poverty. He said Nigeria was close to hyperinflation in 2023, but that critics of hardship are not enemies of the President.
body: The Emir of Kano and former Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) governor, Muhammadu Sanusi II, has urged President Bola Tinubu's government to listen to concerns about poverty rather than treating critics as enemies.
## What he said

Speaking at the Oxford Global Think Tank conference convened by former World Bank vice-president Arunma Oteh, in comments reported on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, Sanusi reportedly said the government's habit of issuing statements from the Presidential Villa to condemn people who raise economic concerns was counterproductive. He argued that citizens who talk about poverty are not attacking the President personally, and that the government should distinguish between criticism and hostility.
## On the economy

Sanusi also said Nigeria was dangerously close to economic collapse in 2023 and on the verge of hyperinflation, a view he said he had held and expressed at the time. His comments suggest he sees the need for reform, while insisting that the hardship many people feel should be acknowledged.
## Background

Sanusi was CBN governor from 2009 to 2014 and is a well-known commentator on the economy. He was reinstated as Emir of Kano in 2024. The Tinubu government removed the petrol subsidy and unified exchange rates in 2023, and says these moves rescued the economy, pointing to falling inflation and rising reserves. Critics, including investment banker Atedo Peterside this week, say the poor have become poorer. Presidency officials have often responded sharply to such criticism, accusing some critics of playing politics ahead of 2027.
## What happens next
The Presidency had not responded to Sanusi's comments at the time of reporting.
more: Sanusi says critics of hardship are not enemies of the President.
He says Nigeria was close to hyperinflation in 2023.
The Presidency has not responded.

stories.h: El-Rufai tells supporters to vote ADC at every level in 2027
stories.p: Former Kaduna governor Nasir El-Rufai has reportedly directed his supporters to back the African Democratic Congress in all elections in 2027. The message was delivered by an ally at a coalition meeting in Kaduna.
body: Former Kaduna State governor Nasir El-Rufai has instructed his supporters to vote for the African Democratic Congress (ADC) at every level in the 2027 elections, according to a close ally.
## The message

Hajiya Hafsat Baba, the ADC's national vice-chairman for the North-West, reportedly conveyed the message at a meeting in Kaduna that brought together various El-Rufai support groups. She said the directive had been verified by El-Rufai himself and covered federal, state and local elections. The meeting was held to unite the groups and coordinate their activities ahead of the polls.
## 'Base still strong'
Another ally, Ibrahim Hussaini, rejected claims that El-Rufai had lost his political base, saying his loyalists remain strong across Kaduna State and the wider North.
## Background

El-Rufai served two terms as governor of Kaduna from 2015 to 2023 as a member of the APC and was a key figure in President Bola Tinubu's 2023 campaign. He later fell out with the party and joined the opposition coalition that adopted the ADC, which has fielded former vice-president Atiku Abubakar as its presidential candidate. His relationship with his successor, Governor Uba Sani of the APC, has been tense. El-Rufai has also been involved in legal disputes in recent months and has appealed for a fair trial.
## Why it matters

Kaduna is one of the most populous states in the North-West, a region with a large share of Nigeria's voters. The APC says it remains strong in the state, while the ADC hopes El-Rufai's support will help it make gains there.
more: The message was relayed by ADC vice-chairman Hafsat Baba.

stories.h: Soludo says his family and Obi's are linked as godparents despite political rift
stories.p: Anambra governor Charles Soludo has reportedly said Peter Obi's wife is godmother to one of his children, and his own wife is confirmation godmother to Obi's daughter. He said their political differences have not broken their friendship.
body: Anambra State governor Charles Soludo has spoken about his close family ties with former governor and NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi, despite their recent political differences.
## What he said

In an interview with a BBC Igbo-language service on Monday, 2 November 2026, Soludo reportedly said that Obi's wife, Margaret, is the godmother of one of his children, and that his own wife, Nonye, is the confirmation godmother of Obi's daughter. He described Obi as a close friend and said no political disagreement had been enough to break the bond between their families.
## Their differences

Soludo said the two men had disagreed on political matters, mainly over who should govern Anambra State. Their relationship became a subject of public debate after a dispute in September, and Soludo has said that his party, APGA, would not automatically support Obi's presidential bid. Soludo has also said he backs President Bola Tinubu for 2027.
## Background

Obi governed Anambra from 2006 to 2014 as a member of APGA, the same party on which Soludo was elected in 2021. Both men are among the most prominent politicians in the South East. Soludo's son, Ozonna, recently released a song supporting the NDC, which drew attention because of his father's backing for Tinubu.
## How people reacted
Many people welcomed the comments as a sign that politics should not destroy friendships, while others said the two men's public differences were more important for voters.
more: Obi's wife is godmother to one of Soludo's children.

stories.h: Wike aide says there is hunger but people are still building houses, sparking debate
stories.p: Lere Olayinka, an aide to FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, has reportedly questioned how young Nigerians describe the level of hardship, pointing to ongoing construction as a sign of economic activity. His comments drew criticism online.
body: Lere Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media to FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, has sparked debate with comments on poverty and hunger in Nigeria.
## What he said

Appearing on a television politics programme, in comments reported on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, Olayinka reportedly pushed back against what he described as the narrative of widespread poverty and hunger promoted by young Nigerians, often referred to as Gen Z. While he acknowledged that people were facing economic pressure, he pointed to private building projects and construction in communities as signs that economic activity was continuing. He said there is hunger, but people are still building houses.
## How people reacted

Many social media users criticised the comments, saying they showed officials were out of touch with ordinary people struggling with high food and transport costs. Others agreed that the economy was not as bad as some critics suggest and said the government's reforms needed time.
## Background

The cost of living is one of the most debated issues ahead of the 2027 elections. On the same day, the Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, urged the government to stop treating talk of poverty as an attack, while investment banker Atedo Peterside said the reforms were making the rich richer and the poor poorer. The government points to falling inflation, a stronger stock market and higher reserves as signs of progress. Wike, a former PDP governor of Rivers State, is a key ally of President Bola Tinubu and leads the Rainbow Coalition backing his re-election.
more: Olayinka pointed to construction as a sign of economic activity.
Many people said the comments were out of touch.
The cost of living is a major 2027 issue.

stories.h: Sola Sobowale opens care home for older people in Ibadan, Makinde commissions it
stories.p: Veteran actress Sola Sobowale has opened Joseph and Esther Homes, a residential care facility for older adults in Akobo, Ibadan. Governor Seyi Makinde commissioned the home, with Nollywood stars in attendance.
body: Veteran Nollywood actress Sola Sobowale has opened a residential care home for older people in Ibadan, Oyo State.
## The opening

Oyo governor Seyi Makinde formally commissioned the facility, named Joseph and Esther Homes, on Tuesday, 3 November 2026. Located in the Akobo area of Ibadan, it is designed to give older adults a safe and supportive place where they can live independently while receiving professional care. The governor toured the indoor and outdoor areas and cut the ribbon.
## The idea behind it

The home operates under the motto 'Live Well, Age Well, Thrive Together'. Its organisers say it is meant to complement family care rather than replace it, helping families look after their elderly relatives better. Formal care homes are still uncommon in Nigeria, where older people have traditionally been cared for at home by relatives.
## Who attended

Sobowale welcomed guests alongside veteran actor Adebayo Salami. Other Nollywood figures at the event included Kunle Afolayan, Femi Adebayo and Ibrahim Chatta. The launch was streamed live on the actress's Instagram page.
## Background
Sola Sobowale is one of Nollywood's most respected actresses, known for her role in the 'King of Boys' films and decades of work in Yoruba and English-language cinema.
## How people reacted
Fans praised the project, saying it addresses a growing need as more young Nigerians move to cities or abroad, leaving ageing parents behind.
more: The home is called Joseph and Esther Homes.
Governor Makinde commissioned it on Tuesday.
Kunle Afolayan and Femi Adebayo attended.

stories.h: Odumodublvck claims some artists turn to spiritual means to get hit songs
stories.p: Rapper Odumodublvck has claimed on a podcast that some Nigerian artists resort to spiritual practices to get hit songs, without naming anyone or giving evidence. He praised Burna Boy, Wizkid and Davido for delivering hits for years.
body: Rapper Odumodublvck, real name Tochukwu Ojogwu, has made a controversial claim about how some musicians chase success in Nigeria's competitive music industry.
## What he said

Speaking on a podcast, in comments shared on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, the rapper said getting a hit song is not easy and that some people even turn to spiritual practices, popularly called 'jazz', to get one. He said this is why some artists appear to struggle badly when they cannot get a hit. He did not name any artist or provide evidence for the claim.
## Praise for the big three

Odumodublvck praised Burna Boy, Wizkid and Davido, saying their ability to release successful songs consistently for years deserves respect. He noted that some artists never get a single hit in their entire careers.
## Background

Odumodublvck rose to fame with his 2023 hit 'Declan Rice' and is known for bold statements. Earlier this week he drew mockery after claiming that Nigerians did not know Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice until he released the song. Claims about artists using spiritual help for success are a long-running topic of gossip in Nigerian entertainment, but they are rarely backed by evidence.
## How people reacted
Fans were divided. Some said the claim reflected what many people already suspect, while others accused the rapper of spreading rumours and said hard work and talent explain most hits.
more: He did not name any artist or give evidence.

stories.h: Atiku accuses DSS of plotting to disrupt ADC rally as Sokoto seals party office
stories.p: ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar has alleged that the DSS is recruiting protesters to disrupt his party's rally in Sokoto. Separately, the Sokoto government sealed an ADC campaign office, saying the building's ownership was unclear and citing a disturbance.
body: Tension is rising in Sokoto State ahead of a planned campaign rally by the African Democratic Congress (ADC), with presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar accusing the Department of State Services (DSS) of plotting to disrupt it.
## Atiku's allegation

In a statement on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, Atiku alleged that the leadership of the DSS was recruiting people to stage protests in Sokoto in order to create disorder. He claimed hired protesters were being gathered at an office on Koko Road and sent out in trucks to key locations in the city. He also said public facilities had been blocked and logistical support withheld to frustrate the ADC's campaign, and warned that security officials who help suppress political freedom would be held to account under the law. He said the rally would go ahead. The DSS had not responded publicly to the claims at the time of reporting.
## Campaign office sealed

Separately, the Sokoto State Government sealed an ADC campaign office on Ahmadu Bello Way on Monday, 2 November. Commissioner for Land and Housing Nasiru Dantsoho said records showed the building, once used by the defunct Savannah Bank and previously by the PDP, still belonged to the bank, and that the state had written to the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation to clarify its ownership. He said the premises were sealed after a disturbance involving party supporters and others, to prevent further trouble. A media aide to the ADC governorship candidate confirmed the closure.
## Background

Sokoto is governed by the APC. Opposition parties have complained of attacks and obstacles to their campaigns in several states, and an ADC candidate's convoy was attacked in Sokoto in recent weeks. The APC and state governments have generally denied using state agencies against opponents.
## What happens next
Security agencies are expected to be on alert as the ADC presses ahead with its rally.
more: Atiku alleges hired protesters are being gathered on Koko Road.
Sokoto sealed an ADC office over ownership questions.

stories.h: Fans raise concern over Doris Ogala's health in detention after medical report surfaces
stories.p: A medical report shared online says actress and governorship aspirant Doris Ogala was treated for severe anaemia linked to a fibroid condition earlier this year, raising concern among supporters about her health in detention. Her bail ruling is due on 6 November.
body: Supporters of actress and governorship aspirant Doris Ogala have raised concerns about her health while she remains in detention, after a medical report about her condition was shared online on Tuesday, 3 November 2026.
## The medical report

According to reports, the document from the Federal Medical Centre in Umuahia, dated 5 June 2026, shows that she was treated for severe anaemia linked to a fibroid condition, following an earlier surgical procedure in 2025. The report reportedly says she was admitted, treated and discharged after significant improvement, and was advised to avoid strenuous activity for six months and attend regular follow-up appointments. Reports claim she has been experiencing renewed bleeding while in detention, but this has not been independently confirmed.
## How people reacted
Fans and supporters took to social media to express worry and call for her release on health grounds. Some urged the authorities to ensure she receives proper medical care while her case continues.
## Background

Doris Ogala, 30, is a Nollywood actress and a governorship candidate of the African Action Congress. She was remanded in custody last month in a case linked to her dispute with Pastor Chris Okafor, which arose from social media posts. The AAC's presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, and other supporters have condemned her detention. A court is due to rule on her bail application on 6 November.
## What happens next
Her lawyers are expected to raise her health when the court considers her bail application.
more: The report says she was treated for severe anaemia earlier this year.
Supporters are calling for her release on health grounds.

stories.h: Rufai Oseni challenges Umahi to win six million votes before comparing himself to Obi
stories.p: TV presenter Rufai Oseni has reportedly hit back at Works Minister Dave Umahi, who called Peter Obi a 'nobody' and described himself as the Lion of the South East. Oseni said Umahi should first run for president and win at least six million votes.
body: Television presenter Rufai Oseni has responded sharply to Minister of Works Dave Umahi's recent comments about NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi.
## What Umahi said

At an APC town hall in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, on Monday, 2 November 2026, Umahi reportedly questioned Obi's political relevance, described him as a 'nobody' and called himself the 'Lion of the South East'. He has also asked what makes Obi better than past South East leaders such as Sam Egwu and Anyim Pius Anyim, and has argued that the region should back President Bola Tinubu so that an Igbo candidate can later get eight years rather than four.
## Oseni's response

Speaking on his breakfast television programme on Tuesday, 3 November, Oseni reportedly said self-given titles mean little without results. He said that before Umahi can compare himself with Obi, he should obtain a presidential nomination form, contest a general election and win at least six million votes, roughly the number Obi received in the 2023 presidential election.
## Background

Umahi, a former two-term governor of Ebonyi State, is a leading APC figure in the South East and has campaigned hard for Tinubu's re-election. Obi, a former Anambra governor, came third in the 2023 presidential election as the Labour Party candidate and is now running on the NDC ticket with Rabiu Kwankwaso. The South East is seen as an important battleground in 2027, and four governors from the zone recently declared support for Tinubu.
## How people reacted
Obi's supporters cheered Oseni's comments, while APC supporters said Umahi's record as governor and minister speaks for itself.
more: Umahi reportedly called Obi a 'nobody' at an Abakaliki town hall.
Oseni says Umahi should first win six million votes.

stories.h: Oyo commissioner and two other officials resign from Makinde government in one day
stories.p: Oyo's Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, a special adviser and an electoral commission member reportedly resigned on Monday. One said he was no longer comfortable with the working environment, adding to a wave of departures before 2027.
body: Three officials serving in Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde's administration resigned on Monday, 2 November 2026, according to reports, in the latest of a series of departures from the state government.
## Who resigned

Those who left were reportedly the Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, Ayobami Ojo; the Special Adviser on Budget and Economic Planning, Adegbola Oyeleke; and Sunday Falana, a member of the Oyo State Independent Electoral Commission. Ojo, who is from Ago-Are in Atisbo Local Government Area, submitted his letter through the Secretary to the State Government, said his exit was with immediate effect and thanked the governor for the opportunity to serve, without giving a reason. Oyeleke reportedly said he was no longer comfortable with the working environment in the administration.
## Background

Makinde is serving his second and final term as governor and is now the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) for 2027. Several officials have left his government in recent months as politicians reposition ahead of the elections, with some moving to rival parties. The governor has not publicly commented on the latest resignations.
## Why it matters
The departures come as Makinde campaigns nationally, including in the South East, and as parties compete for control of Oyo State, where the governorship seat will be open in 2027.
more: The budget commissioner, a special adviser and an OYSIEC member resigned.
One official cited the working environment.
Makinde has not commented.

stories.h: No Nigerian on CAF Women's Player of the Year shortlist for the first time
stories.p: For the first time since the award began in 2001, no Nigerian player is on CAF's shortlist for Women's Player of the Year. The Super Falcons are still nominated for National Team of the Year, and three Nigerians made other lists.
body: Nigeria has no player on the shortlist for the 2026 CAF Women's Player of the Year award, the first time the country has been left out since the prize was introduced in 2001, according to reports.
## The nominees

The Confederation of African Football released the nominations this week. The list includes Malawian sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga, Cameroon's Marie Ngah Manga, Michaely Bihina and Monique Ngock, Zambia's Barbra Banda, South Africa's Thembi Kgatlana, Morocco's Hanane Ait El Haj, Algeria's Marine Dafeur and Ghana's Portia Boakye.
## Nigerians on other lists

Nigeria still features in other categories. The Super Falcons were shortlisted for Women's National Team of the Year, Janet Akekoromowei and Oluwakemi Adegbuyi were nominated for the young talent award, and Edo Queens goalkeeper Christiana Uzoma is among the contenders for Goalkeeper of the Year.
## Background

Nigerian players have dominated the award over the years, with Asisat Oshoala winning it a record six times. The omission follows a disappointing 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations for the Super Falcons and their failure to qualify for the Women's World Cup for the first time. The team only this week received the cash rewards promised for winning the previous WAFCON.
## What happens next
The 2026 CAF Awards will be held on 7 December at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts in Lagos.
more: It is the first time since 2001 that no Nigerian made the list.
The Super Falcons are nominated for Team of the Year.
The awards hold on 7 December.

stories.h: Portugal moves to double citizenship wait to 10 years for Nigerians and others
stories.p: Portugal has approved regulations to apply its amended nationality law, which raises the minimum legal residence for citizenship from five to 10 years for nationals of countries including Nigeria. EU and Portuguese-speaking nationals face seven years.
body: Portugal is moving ahead with stricter citizenship rules that will double the waiting time for Nigerians and many other foreign residents, according to reports.
## What changed

Portugal's Council of Ministers approved regulations on 29 October 2026 to put the country's amended Nationality Law into effect. Under the revised law, the minimum period of legal residence before applying for citizenship rises from five to 10 years for nationals of countries including Nigeria, India, Pakistan, Nepal and Bangladesh. Citizens of European Union countries and of Portuguese-speaking countries such as Angola, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, São Tomé and Príncipe and Mozambique will have a seven-year route. The regulations also set out how language skills, cultural knowledge and financial independence will be assessed.
## Not yet final
As of 2 November, the implementing decree had reportedly not yet been published in the official gazette, so some details of how the rules will apply remain unclear.
## Background

Portugal has become a popular destination for migrants, including Nigerians, because of its relatively open residence routes. The government says the changes are meant to strengthen integration, while critics say they will make life harder for long-term residents. Hundreds of thousands of citizenship applications are reportedly waiting to be processed.
## Why it matters
The change is the latest in a series of tighter immigration rules in Europe. This week the UK also confirmed a 10-year route to settlement for most lower-paid migrants.
more: The minimum residence rises from five to 10 years for Nigerians.
EU and Portuguese-speaking nationals get a seven-year route.
The decree had not yet been published as of 2 November.

stories.h: Naira weakens in October as dollar demand outstrips CBN's $1.98bn intervention
stories.p: The naira lost about 1.3% against the dollar in October, ending three months of gains, as festive-season demand and dollar shortages pressured the market. The CBN injected nearly $2 billion but reportedly met demand fully in only two of five interventions.
body: Nigeria's currency has come under fresh pressure as businesses scramble for dollars ahead of the festive season, according to market data reported on Tuesday, 3 November 2026.
## The numbers

The naira closed October at ₦1,346.91 per dollar on the official market, compared with ₦1,329.50 at the end of September, a fall of about 1.31 per cent. It was the first monthly decline after three consecutive months of gains. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) reportedly injected about $1.98 billion into the market during the month, but demand was fully met in only two of its five interventions.
## Why it is happening

Importers, manufacturers and traders typically need more foreign currency towards the end of the year to bring in goods for Christmas and New Year sales. Analysts say this seasonal demand, combined with limited dollar inflows, is putting pressure on the naira.
## What it means

A weaker naira raises the cost of imported goods and raw materials, which can push up prices for consumers. The CBN says stronger dollar inflows from oil exports, foreign investment and remittances are key to keeping the currency stable.
## Background

The naira has been more stable in recent months after sharp falls in 2023 and 2024 following the unification of exchange rates. Foreign reserves have risen to their highest level in years, and inflation has fallen. The government points to these gains as evidence that its reforms are working, while critics say ordinary Nigerians are still struggling with high prices.
more: The naira fell about 1.31% in October.
The CBN injected nearly $2 billion.
Festive-season demand is adding pressure.

stories.h: "Men, I finally understand what you go through, and I'm sorry": American hip-hop artist Rayven Tyler speaks on dating women
stories.p: American hip-hop artist Rayven Tyler has sparked conversation about relationships after saying that dating women has helped her understand some of the challenges men face in romantic relationships, and apologising to men.
body: American hip-hop artist Rayven Tyler has sparked conversation about relationships after sharing her experience of dating women and admitting that she now understands some of the challenges men face.
## What she said
According to the artist, her personal experiences have given her a different perspective on dating, and made her appreciate what many men go through when trying to keep their relationships going.
"After dating women for so long, I just want to say I get it now, men, and I'm sorry. Now I know what you guys are passing through," she reportedly said.
## Why it struck a chord
For years, men have complained about the pressures they face in relationships, from managing emotional expectations to dealing with misunderstandings and trying to keep their partners happy.

Tyler's statement suggests that her own dating experiences have helped her see some of those complaints from a different angle. What makes her comments particularly interesting is that she is speaking from her own experience of dating women, a perspective that has drawn plenty of attention.
Her remarks have opened a wider discussion about emotional expectations, communication and the difficulties that sometimes come with understanding a partner.
## Every relationship is different
Relationship experiences differ from person to person, and her comments reflect her own perspective rather than the behaviour of all women.
## Over to you
Does dating women give women a better understanding of what men experience in relationships, or does everything depend on the individual involved?
more: Rayven Tyler says dating women changed her view of men's struggles.
She apologised to men in a video.
Her comments reflect her personal experience.

stories.h: Regina Daniels shares fresh Snapchat video, appears to be doing better
stories.p: Nollywood actress Regina Daniels seems to be gradually getting back to her usual self, judging by a new video she shared on Snapchat. She appeared cheerful and relaxed in the clip, although she has not given any detailed update on her situation.
body: Nollywood actress Regina Daniels seems to be gradually getting back to her usual self, judging by a new video she shared on Snapchat this morning.
## The new video

The actress, who has been attracting a lot of public attention lately, appeared in the fresh clip looking cheerful and relaxed. The video, posted from Abuja in the early hours of 3 November, shows her in a black and pink outfit, moving casually at home.
## No detailed update yet

Regina has not given any detailed update about her current situation. Even so, her latest appearance suggests she may be in better spirits, and many fans have welcomed seeing her looking more like herself again.
## What comes next

Regina Daniels has been one of Nollywood's most talked-about stars since she rose to fame as a child actress, and her personal life has often drawn as much attention as her films. Fans will certainly be watching to see what comes next as she continues to share glimpses of her life on social media.
What do you make of Regina's latest video?

stories.h: "I am broken, I now understand the pain I once mocked": Blessing CEO apologises, says she is returning like the prodigal son
stories.p: Controversial relationship therapist Blessing CEO has shared an emotional message of regret, apologising to people she may have offended in the past. She described herself as broken and compared her journey to the biblical story of the prodigal son.
body: Controversial relationship therapist Blessing CEO has shared an emotional message of regret, apologising to people she may have offended through her words and actions in the past.
## "I now understand the pain I once mocked"

In her statement, Blessing admitted that she once spoke carelessly about people's struggles without fully understanding what they were going through. Now, according to her, life has placed her in a position where she can finally relate to some of that pain.
She described herself as emotionally broken, saying her present struggles have left her feeling lost and surrounded by darkness.
## Like the prodigal son
Blessing also compared her situation to the biblical story of the prodigal son, who returned home after going through difficult experiences.
Her words suggest a period of deep personal reflection, as she acknowledges past mistakes and expresses a desire to make peace with those she may have hurt.
## A change in tone
For someone who built a reputation on speaking boldly about relationships, personal struggles and other people's choices, this public apology marks a noticeable change in tone.
Sometimes, life has a way of teaching people lessons they once thought they already understood.
## Over to you
Has Blessing CEO genuinely turned a new leaf, or is this another emotional chapter in her controversial public life?
What do you think?

stories.h: Super Falcons finally receive $100,000 each for 2024 WAFCON win
stories.p: Players of the Super Falcons have reportedly started receiving the naira equivalent of $100,000 each, the reward President Tinubu promised after their record 10th WAFCON title. Members of the technical crew are getting $50,000 each.
body: Members of Nigeria's Super Falcons have reportedly begun receiving the cash reward promised by President Bola Tinubu after the team won the 2024 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON).
## What happened

According to reports, two players and a member of the technical crew confirmed that their accounts were credited on Monday, 2 November 2026. Each of the 24 players is said to have received the naira equivalent of $100,000, about ₦140 million, while each of the 11 members of the technical crew received the naira equivalent of $50,000. One player reportedly said she was grateful that the promise had finally been kept.
## Other rewards
Apart from the cash, the President also approved national honours and three-bedroom apartments for the players and officials after the victory.
## Background

The Super Falcons won a record-extending 10th continental title in Morocco in July 2025, coming from behind to beat the hosts in the final. The tournament, originally scheduled for 2024, was held a year later but kept its 2024 name. The win was celebrated across Nigeria, and the team was received by the President at the State House, where the rewards were announced. Delays in paying promised bonuses to national teams have been a long-running complaint in Nigerian sport, and some fans had questioned whether this reward would ever be paid.
## How people reacted

Fans welcomed the news, saying the players deserved the money and calling on the government to pay other national teams promptly in future. Others said the long delay showed the need for clear and timely reward systems.
more: Each of the 24 players reportedly received about ₦140 million.
Technical crew members got $50,000 each.

stories.h: Cooking gas depot prices jump by up to 16% in three days
stories.p: Cooking gas prices at major Lagos depots reportedly rose by between ₦140 and ₦200 per kilogram between 30 October and 2 November. Navgas listed the highest price at ₦1,450 per kg, while Dangote had the lowest at ₦1,050.
body: Nigerians are facing higher cooking gas costs after depot prices at major suppliers in Lagos rose sharply in just three days, according to a price review published on Monday, 2 November 2026.
## The new prices

All five monitored Lagos depots reportedly raised their prices between 30 October and 2 November, with increases of ₦140 to ₦200 per kilogram. Navgas recorded the steepest rise, from ₦1,250 to ₦1,450 per kg, an increase of 16 per cent. 11Plc and Nipco both moved from ₦1,225 to ₦1,390 per kg, while Techno Oil and Rain Oil went from ₦1,200 to ₦1,370 per kg. Dangote's depot price was the lowest among those monitored, at ₦1,050 per kg.
## What it means for households

Depot prices feed directly into what retailers charge for refilling cylinders, so consumers are likely to pay more in the coming days. A 12.5kg cylinder, the size used by many families, could cost roughly ₦2,000 more to refill at these depot rates. Clean cooking advocates warned that rising gas costs are pushing some households back to firewood and charcoal, which are cheaper but cause indoor air pollution and deforestation.
## Background

Cooking gas prices in Nigeria have been volatile over the past two years, affected by exchange rates, supply problems and international prices. The government has encouraged wider use of liquefied petroleum gas as a cleaner alternative to kerosene and firewood. The Dangote refinery has also become a major supplier, and its prices have often been lower than those of other depots.
## What happens next
Marketers say prices will depend on supply and global market conditions in the coming weeks.
more: Depot prices rose by ₦140–₦200 per kg in three days.

stories.h: Blessing CEO apologises in tearful video weeks after son's death
stories.p: Relationship influencer Blessing CEO has shared an emotional video apologising to everyone she has hurt with her words, saying she now feels the pain she once spoke about carelessly. She is mourning her nine-year-old son, who died while she was in custody.
body: Social media personality Nkiru Blessing Okoro, known as Blessing CEO, has issued an emotional public apology, weeks after the death of her nine-year-old son.
## The video

In a video posted on Instagram on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, the relationship influencer was seen crying inside a parked car. She said she had gone there because she did not want her mother to see her in that state. She described feeling confused, numb, broken and surrounded by darkness, and said she was so exhausted that she needed people to pray for her.
## Her apology

Blessing CEO apologised to everyone she had hurt with her words and actions, saying she had spoken carelessly about pain she had never experienced and could now feel the pain she once mocked. She said she was only human and bound to make mistakes, and compared herself to the prodigal son returning home. She also thanked those who still love her and apologised to those who no longer do.
## Background

Her son, Bryan, died from an asthma attack while she was being held in custody in Lagos, according to reports. She was later released on bail and is facing a court case, which is still ongoing. Since her release she has spoken about her ordeal and denied rumours about drug use. Before her troubles, she was known for strong and often controversial relationship advice online, which drew both followers and critics.
## How people reacted
Many social media users expressed sympathy and prayed for her healing, while some said her apology showed growth. Others urged people to stop mocking her and to respect a grieving mother.
more: She said she now feels the pain she once spoke about carelessly.
Her nine-year-old son died while she was in custody.

stories.h: Odion Ighalo says he has paid tithe since his first ₦15,000 salary, sparks debate
stories.p: Former Super Eagles striker Odion Ighalo has reportedly said he has never missed paying tithe since his first salary in 2005, even when he earned $642,000 a month in Saudi Arabia. His comments have divided opinion online.
body: Former Super Eagles striker Odion Ighalo has started a lively online debate after speaking about his long commitment to paying tithes.
## What he said

In a podcast-style interview, reportedly shared on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, Ighalo said he began paying tithe in 2005 when he received his first professional salary of ₦15,000, after his pastor introduced him to the practice, and that he has not missed it since. He admitted that the habit became harder when his income grew. When he was earning a reported $642,000 a month in Saudi Arabia, about ₦900 million at today's exchange rate, he said he thought about it for around a month before deciding to continue paying 10 per cent. He said some friends had questioned his decision, but he stood by it.
## Background

Ighalo, 37, played for clubs including Watford and Manchester United before moving to Saudi Arabia, where he became one of the best-paid African players. He was top scorer at the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations and has long spoken publicly about his Christian faith.
## How people reacted

Opinion was divided. Many Christians praised his faith and discipline and said his success was a blessing. Others argued that giving such large sums to churches was unnecessary and that the money could do more good if given directly to people in need. Some said it was his personal choice and others should respect it.
## Why it matters
Tithing is a frequent topic of debate in Nigeria, where churches play a large role in public life and some pastors have faced criticism over their wealth.
more: Ighalo says he has paid tithe since his first ₦15,000 salary.

stories.h: Deposed Ipetumodu monarch sues Adeleke to stop appointment of successor
stories.p: Oba Joseph Oloyede, removed as Apetumodu of Ipetumodu after his conviction in the US for fraud, has reportedly asked an Osun High Court to stop Governor Ademola Adeleke from filling the stool. The case was adjourned to 21 January 2027.
body: The deposed Apetumodu of Ipetumodu in Osun State, Oba Joseph Oloyede, has gone to court to stop Governor Ademola Adeleke from appointing a new traditional ruler for the town.
## The case

According to reports, Oloyede filed a motion at the Osun State High Court in Ile-Ife asking the court to restrain the governor and other officials from filling the stool until his main case is decided. In the application, dated 16 September 2026, he argued that he was not formally told of any wrongdoing before he was removed, and challenged the legality of his deposition. Members of a branch of the town's ruling house joined him as claimants. The defendants include the governor, the state Attorney-General, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, local chiefs and Ife North Local Government.
## What happened in court

Proceedings stalled on Monday, 2 November, after some defendants said they had not received hearing notices. Justice Dapo Adeniji adjourned the case to 21 January 2027 and ordered that fresh notices be served.
## Background

Oloyede was removed from the throne after he was convicted in the United States on charges related to tax fraud and money laundering. Governor Adeleke reportedly signed the order removing him in May 2026.
## What happens next
The court will hear the case in January. Until then, it is not clear whether the state will go ahead with appointing a new monarch.
more: He says he was not told of any wrongdoing before his removal.
He was removed after a US conviction for tax fraud and money laundering.

stories.h: US reportedly carries out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on eve of midterms
stories.p: US officials say American forces carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, in response to Iranian missile fire at US assets. Iranian state media reported explosions, while Iran claimed it captured two US drones.
body: The United States military has reportedly carried out limited strikes on Qeshm Island, a strategic Iranian island near the Strait of Hormuz, on Monday, 2 November 2026, the eve of the US midterm elections.
## What happened

According to US officials quoted in reports, the operation was a defensive response after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) fired surface-to-air missiles at US assets. Iranian state media confirmed several explosions on the island. Officials reportedly said it was one of a series of low-profile strikes carried out in recent weeks, kept quiet to avoid signalling a return to full-scale fighting. Separately, the IRGC claimed it had intercepted and captured two US drones south of Qeshm.
## Why Qeshm matters

Qeshm is the largest island in the Persian Gulf and is said to hold Iranian anti-ship missiles, sea mines and drones in underground tunnels. Its position near the Strait of Hormuz, through which a large share of the world's oil passes, makes it militarily important.
## Diplomacy continues

The strikes came as Qatar leads indirect talks between the two sides. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, described the talks as active, and on Monday Iran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US met its conditions. US Vice President JD Vance reportedly said there had been progress, but warned that Iran remains unpredictable and that President Donald Trump would keep both military and diplomatic options open.
## Why it matters

Oil prices rose slightly after reports of the strikes, with Brent crude trading at about $105 a barrel. Higher oil prices affect Nigeria's revenue and fuel costs around the world. The conflict between the US and Iran began on 28 February.
more: US officials called it a defensive response to Iranian missile fire.

stories.h: US to remove South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA duty-free trade scheme
stories.p: The US says it will remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act from 1 January 2027, accusing both of practices that break the scheme's rules. South Africa says it will support affected industries.
body: The United States plans to remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), its main duty-free trade programme for African countries, from 1 January 2027.
## What the US said

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Monday, 2 November 2026, that President Donald Trump intends to end the two countries' participation in the scheme. According to reports, Greer said the President found that both governments were engaging in practices inconsistent with AGOA's eligibility rules, including barriers to American trade and investment and actions that threaten US security and foreign policy interests in the region.
## South Africa's response

South Africa's trade ministry said it would support the sectors affected and would keep pursuing trade and investment with the United States. It said AGOA remains important but is not the whole of the economic relationship between the two countries.
## What is at stake

AGOA, enacted in 2000, gives eligible African countries duty-free access to the US market for thousands of products. South Africa has been its largest beneficiary, exporting about $1.7 billion worth of goods under the scheme in 2025, mainly car parts, citrus fruit and wine. Rwanda's main exports include coffee and minerals.
## Background

The Trump administration has taken a series of steps against South Africa, accusing its government of persecuting white South Africans, a claim Pretoria rejects. Nigeria remains an AGOA beneficiary, although its exports under the scheme are dominated by oil. Trade experts say the decision is a warning to other African countries that eligibility can be withdrawn.
more: The suspension takes effect on 1 January 2027.
South Africa exported about $1.7 billion under AGOA in 2025.

stories.h: Atiku's campaign says Umrah will not win Tinubu a second term
stories.p: A spokesman for Atiku Abubakar's campaign has reportedly said President Tinubu's Umrah trip will not secure his re-election, arguing that voters will judge him on the cost of living. Tinubu said he went to give thanks, as he did before the 2023 election.
body: The campaign of African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar says President Bola Tinubu's recent Umrah in Saudi Arabia will not guarantee him a second term.
## What was said

Speaking on a television politics programme on Monday night, 2 November 2026, Phrank Shaibu, director of strategic communication for the ADC presidential campaign council, reportedly said political mandates cannot be won through religious display. He argued that pilgrimage should be a personal matter, not something publicised as a national event by political supporters, and said Nigerians would make their choice in 2027 based on the cost of living rather than prayers abroad. Asked whether Atiku would have joined Tinubu if invited, he said the former vice-president had supported Tinubu's earlier trips to Mecca. He also claimed Atiku was in a strong position in the North.
## The President's side

Tinubu left Abuja for Makkah on 29 October. He described the trip as a chance to seek divine guidance, wisdom and resilience, and said that before the 2023 election he had performed Umrah and promised to return to give thanks if his prayers were answered. During the visit he was granted the rare privilege of entering the Kaaba, where he said he prayed for peace, unity and prosperity for Nigeria. The Presidency has rejected claims that the trip was for medical reasons.
## Background

The trip has drawn comment across the political spectrum. Former senator Dino Melaye challenged Tinubu to a Quran recitation contest, while Oyo governor Seyi Makinde asked the Presidency to explain the purpose of the journey. APC supporters have welcomed the visit and the honour extended by the Saudi leadership.
more: The ADC says voters will judge Tinubu on the cost of living.
Tinubu said he went to give thanks, as he did before 2023.

stories.h: Video of Catholic priest leading campaign song for Obi and Kwankwaso goes viral
stories.p: A video showing a Catholic priest leading his congregation in an Igbo song praising Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso's party during a Sunday service has gone viral. It adds to debate over religious leaders taking sides ahead of 2027.
body: A video of a Catholic priest leading worshippers in a song backing NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi and his running mate Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has spread widely on social media.
## What the video shows

In the clip, reportedly filmed during a Sunday service, the priest leads the congregation in an Igbo song saying the party of Obi and Kwankwaso is better, and the worshippers sing along. The priest's name and the location of the church have not been confirmed. The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), which ratified Obi as its presidential candidate in May, shared the video.
## Religious leaders and politics

The video comes as religious leaders across Nigeria increasingly declare support for or against candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. According to reports, a separate bishops' conference has endorsed President Bola Tinubu for a second term, while an Islamic cleric was reported to have urged Muslims to vote along religious lines. Last week, a Catholic bishop warned politicians against trying to manipulate the electoral system, and a priest urged Nigerians to collect their voter cards instead of complaining.
## How people reacted

Obi's supporters celebrated the video, while critics said churches should not be used for partisan campaigns and warned that such displays could deepen religious and ethnic divisions. Others said priests, like all citizens, are entitled to their political views.
## Background
Electoral rules prohibit the use of places of worship for political campaigns, although enforcement has historically been rare. The Catholic Church has not publicly commented on the video.
more: The priest led an Igbo song praising Obi and Kwankwaso's party.
A separate bishops' conference has endorsed Tinubu.

stories.h: Atedo Peterside says Tinubu's reforms are making the rich richer and the poor poorer
stories.p: Investment banker Atedo Peterside has reportedly said the government's economic reforms are benefiting wealthier Nigerians with investments while low-income workers are worse off. He said his concern is for the more than 130 million Nigerians who are poor.
body: Investment banker and IBTC founder Atedo Peterside says the Tinubu administration's economic reforms are widening the gap between rich and poor Nigerians.
## What he said

Speaking in a television interview on Monday night, 2 November 2026, Peterside reportedly said that whether the reforms are working depends on who is asked. He said upper-middle-class Nigerians with investments in the stock market are probably better off than they were three years ago, while low-income workers with little savings who struggle to eat two meals a day and pay their bills are a lot worse off. He admitted that his own investment income had risen, but said his concern was for the 130 to 140 million Nigerians who are poor and getting poorer.
## Background

The government removed the petrol subsidy and unified the exchange rate in 2023, moves that pushed up prices but which it says were needed to rescue the economy. Officials point to falling inflation, which dropped to 14.63 per cent in September, rising foreign reserves and a stock market that hit a record high last week. Critics say these gains have not yet reached ordinary households, many of whom still struggle with high food and transport costs.
## Political debate

The state of the economy is a central issue in the 2027 campaign. Opposition candidates say the reforms have made life harder, while the government says it is cushioning the poor through cash transfers and credit schemes.
more: Peterside says investors are better off, low-income workers worse off.

stories.h: Tanzania head to Uyo early for Super Eagles AFCON qualifier
stories.p: Tanzania's national team is reportedly arriving early in Uyo to prepare for their 2027 AFCON qualifier against the Super Eagles on Friday, 13 November. The sides meet again in Dar es Salaam four days later.
body: Tanzania's national team, the Taifa Stars, are set to arrive early in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, ahead of their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Nigeria's Super Eagles, according to reports.
## The fixtures

Nigeria will host the matchday three game at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on Friday, 13 November 2026. The two teams will meet again four days later in Dar es Salaam for the matchday four fixture.
## Tanzania's preparations

Head coach Miguel Gamondi reportedly wants extra time for his players to get used to conditions in Nigeria before the game. He has named a 24-man squad split evenly between 12 home-based players and 12 who play abroad.
## Background

The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations will be co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. The Super Eagles need good results in the double-header to stay on course for the tournament. Uyo has become the Super Eagles' main home ground in recent years and is known for its passionate crowds. The confederation recently confirmed Nigerian Samson Adamu as its General Secretary and voted to return the Nations Cup to a two-year cycle.
## What happens next
The Super Eagles are expected to open camp in Uyo next week, with fans looking forward to two important results.
more: Nigeria host Tanzania in Uyo on Friday, 13 November.
The return game is in Dar es Salaam four days later.

stories.h: Government opens new round of free vocational training with ₦30,000 monthly stipend
stories.p: The federal government has reportedly opened applications for Batch C of its TVET initiative, offering free training in trades such as solar installation, plumbing and fashion design, plus a ₦30,000 monthly stipend. Applications are free on the official portal.
body: The federal government has opened applications for the third batch of its Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) initiative, which offers free skills training and a monthly stipend, according to reports on Monday, 2 November 2026.
## What is on offer

The programme, coordinated by the Federal Ministry of Education, provides free vocational training at accredited technical colleges, government institutions and registered private centres across the country. Participants receive ₦30,000 a month throughout their training. Trades on offer reportedly include solar installation, plumbing, fashion design and car repairs.
## Two training options

Applicants can choose a six-month short-term certificate course aimed at beginners, school leavers and people without formal qualifications, or a one-year vocational education and innovation course for those with previous education or informal training in a trade.
## How to apply

Applications are free and are made through the official TVET portal. No closing date has been announced, so applicants are advised to watch for official updates and to avoid anyone asking for money to register.
## Background

The initiative was launched to tackle youth unemployment and the country's skills gap by training young Nigerians in practical trades that are in demand. Earlier batches attracted large numbers of applicants. The scheme is one of several government programmes aimed at easing hardship, alongside cash transfers and consumer credit.
more: Participants get ₦30,000 a month during training.
Courses last six months or one year.
Applications are free on the official portal.

stories.h: Police officers feared dead as bandits ambush bus heading to Zamfara APC primary
stories.p: Bandits ambushed a bus carrying police officers on the Sokoto–Gusau road in Zamfara State on Monday. The officers were travelling to provide security for an APC senatorial primary, and some are feared dead while others were reportedly abducted.
body: Several police officers are feared dead after suspected bandits attacked a bus carrying them along the Sokoto–Gusau road in Zamfara State on Monday, 2 November 2026.
## What happened

The officers were travelling in a state mass transit bus, known locally as Bazamfara, towards Gusau, the state capital. According to police sources, they were on their way to provide security for the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for the Zamfara North senatorial district, which was taking place in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. Sources said some officers were killed in the ambush and others were abducted by the attackers. The exact number of casualties had not been confirmed at the time of reporting.
## Official response

The spokesman for the police zone covering the area reportedly confirmed the attack, but said he was in hospital and would issue an official statement later. The identities of the victims have not been released.
## Background

Zamfara is one of the states worst affected by banditry in north-west Nigeria, with frequent attacks on travellers, villages and security personnel. Police officers are often deployed to provide security at party primaries and campaign events, and several political gatherings have been attacked in recent weeks as the 2027 elections approach. In neighbouring Niger State, gunmen abducted 14 Islamiyya students and their teacher at the weekend.
## Primary result

The primary went ahead despite the attack. The APC later declared Sahabi Ya'u Kaura the winner of the fresh Zamfara North senatorial primary, held after a court invalidated the earlier exercise. He reportedly polled 49,176 votes, ahead of Tijjani Kaura with 9,628 and Abdullahi Sani Shinkafi with 6,206, winning in all four local government areas.
## What happens next
Security agencies are expected to launch an operation to rescue the abducted officers, and the police are expected to release casualty figures.
more: The officers were going to provide security at an APC primary.
Some officers were reportedly abducted.
Police say an official statement will follow.

stories.h: Gunmen abduct 14 Islamiyya students and their teacher on Niger farm
stories.p: Police in Niger State say suspected bandits abducted 14 Islamiyya students and their teacher while they were harvesting maize on a farm in Rafi Local Government Area. Police corrected earlier reports that 50 pupils were taken.
body: Suspected bandits have abducted 14 students of an Islamic school and their teacher in Rafi Local Government Area of Niger State, police have confirmed.
## What happened

The attack happened at about 12.30pm on Saturday, 31 October 2026, in Tungan-Bako village near Pandogari. According to the police, the students were helping their teacher harvest maize on his farm when armed men stormed the area and took them away.
## Police statement

The spokesman for the Niger State Police Command, Wasiu Abiodun, confirmed the incident on Monday, 2 November. He said the number of students abducted was 14, correcting earlier reports that about 50 pupils had been seized. He said a joint team of security forces had been deployed to rescue the victims and that further updates would be given.
## Background

Rafi and nearby local government areas in Niger State have suffered repeated attacks by armed groups in recent years, including mass abductions from schools and villages. Kidnapping for ransom remains a serious problem across north-west and north-central Nigeria, and farmers are often targeted during the harvest season. On the same day the abduction was confirmed, bandits ambushed a bus carrying police officers in neighbouring Zamfara State.
## What happens next
Families and community leaders are calling for the quick and safe release of the students.
more: The students were harvesting maize on their teacher's farm.
Police say 14 students were taken, not 50.
A joint rescue operation is under way.

stories.h: Eedris Abdulkareem releases new song asking Seyi Tinubu to plead with his father
stories.p: Veteran rapper Eedris Abdulkareem has reportedly released a new music video in which he addresses Seyi Tinubu, asking him to beg his father, President Tinubu, to ease Nigerians' hardship. He also criticised the new tax law and the electoral system.
body: Veteran rapper Eedris Abdulkareem has released a new song with a pointed political message for President Bola Tinubu, this time delivered through the President's son, Seyi Tinubu.
## The song

In a music video posted on Instagram on Monday, 2 November 2026, Eedris reportedly addresses Seyi directly, asking him to plead with his father on behalf of Nigerians. The lyrics contrast the President's role as a good father to his own family with what the rapper describes as hardship for ordinary Nigerians. According to reports, the song also takes aim at the National Assembly over the newly passed tax law and criticises the electoral system.
## Background

Eedris, best known for his 2004 hit 'Jaga Jaga', has used music to criticise Nigerian governments for more than two decades. In 2025 he released a song critical of the Tinubu government, which the broadcasting regulator restricted on air. On Monday he also denied claims that he had joined the APC, accusing Isaac Fayose of hypocrisy for saying so. Seyi Tinubu has become a visible figure in his father's re-election campaign, and the Presidency has defended the government's reforms, saying they are needed to fix the economy.
## How people reacted

The video drew strong reactions online. Many fans praised the rapper for speaking up about the cost of living, while supporters of the President accused him of playing politics ahead of the 2027 elections.
## What happens next
Neither Seyi Tinubu nor the Presidency had responded publicly at the time of reporting.
more: Eedris addresses Seyi Tinubu directly in the lyrics.
The song also criticises the new tax law.
The Presidency has not responded.

stories.h: Government credit agency launches SPARK scheme for buying food and solar on credit
stories.p: The Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation has reportedly launched SPARK, a scheme to help Nigerians buy food, solar systems and other household goods on credit, including through a USSD code. It says over 351,000 people have accessed more than ₦53.5 billion in credit so far.
body: The Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP), a federal government agency, has launched a new scheme called SPARK to help Nigerians buy essential goods on credit, according to reports on Monday, 2 November 2026.
## What SPARK offers

The scheme is designed to let people buy items such as food, solar power systems and other household needs without paying the full amount upfront. It also aims to support Nigerian businesses and manufacturers by boosting demand for locally made goods. Reports say Nigerians will be able to access the service through a USSD code, which works on basic phones without internet access.
## The numbers so far
CREDICORP says it has facilitated more than ₦53.5 billion in consumer credit for over 351,000 Nigerians since it began operations, and that women make up about 59 per cent of beneficiaries.
## A loan, not a grant

Applicants are being reminded that SPARK is a loan that must be repaid, not free money. People are advised to check the official terms, use only official channels and beware of fraudsters who may pretend to offer access to the scheme for a fee.
## Background

CREDICORP was set up in 2024 as part of President Tinubu's plan to make consumer credit more widely available, so that working Nigerians can buy goods such as cars, homes and appliances and pay over time. Critics have questioned how many people can afford new debt at a time of high living costs, while supporters say affordable credit can ease pressure on household budgets.
more: SPARK lets people buy food and solar systems on credit.
Over 351,000 Nigerians have accessed ₦53.5 billion so far.
It is a loan that must be repaid.
